conventions.convention: Spacetime is Q = I × Ω, with time first. Distribution pairings are bilinear without complex conjugation; a derivative acts by minus the corresponding test derivative.

The entropy residual is nonpositive. Equivalently, the entropy-density/test-time-derivative plus entropy-flux/test-space-derivative integral is nonnegative for nonnegative tests, including the initial entropy term when applicable.
The interface is n·x − st = 0 with |n| = 1; the minus side has n·x − st < 0, and [G] = G_R − G_L. Traces come from local C1 side extensions, independently of assigned interface values.

δΣ integrates dt times spatial plane Lebesgue measure, parametrized by x = Ez + stn for a linear isometry E onto n⊥. It is not unnormalized spacetime surface measure. In dimension one the spatial singleton has mass one. Countable Choice is assumed.
Eigenvalues are ordered increasingly. A k-Lax shock satisfies λk(U_R) < s < λk(U_L), with λk−1(U_L) < s and s < λk+1(U_R) when those indices exist.

Initial-boundary tests may be nonzero at t = 0 and have compact support in [0,T) × Ω. The Riemann theorem assumes F'' > 0 on the closed interval between distinct states and uses sgn(0) = 0 for Kružkov fluxes.

load_bearing.statement: Defines distributional conservation systems for C1 fluxes on an open convex state domain, compatible convex C2 entropy-flux pairs, the nonpositive entropy-residual convention, and initial-value weak and entropy identities.

Assuming Countable Choice, a locally integrable piecewise C1 field solving the conservation system classically on both sides of n·x = st has distributional residual (Σj n_j[F_j(U)] − s[U])δΣ, with the explicitly defined plane measure. It solves the distributional system if and only if s[U] = Σj n_j[F_j(U)] at every interface point.

Assuming Countable Choice and the stated piecewise C1 classical equations, local integrability and entropy compatibility, the entropy residual is (Σj n_j[q_j(U)] − s[η(U)])δΣ. The entropy inequality holds near the interface if and only if this coefficient is nonpositive at every interface point.

Assuming Countable Choice, F ∈ C2(R), and F'' > 0 on the closed interval between distinct states a,b, the specified constant, decreasing-state shock, or increasing-state inverse-characteristic fan satisfies the initial weak identity and every stated convex C2 and Kružkov entropy inequality. The fan has equality; the shock satisfies F'(b) < s < F'(a). No general existence or uniqueness claim is made.
Let Ω ⊆ Rⁿ be open and let f ∈ L1_loc(Ω; C). The regular functional ⟨T_f,φ⟩ = ∫Ω fφ is a distribution on Ω with the LF test-function topology.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 passes to the limit in the full initial-boundary test integral using L1_loc convergence only on (0,T) × Ω. Such convergence directly controls compact sets bounded away from t = 0, not the whole test support. The missing argument is short: split at t = δ, use the assumed convergence on the remaining compact slab, and bound the omitted strip uniformly by Cδ using the common range bound and bounded test derivatives; then send δ to zero.

alerts.finding: Proof 1.2 says u(ε,x) 'differs from f(x) only between the rays x=u_Lε and x=u_Rε, an interval of length (u_R-u_L)ε'; Proof 4.1 repeats that support-length assertion. For u_L=1,u_R=2, the profile also differs from the initial step on 0<x<ε. The containing interval must include zero, for example [min(0,u_Lε), max(0,u_Rε)]. The trace conclusion remains valid with the corrected O(ε) bound; the assigned local fan proof already uses it.
